FOGGARA-DZ / An Algerian platform initiative with national scope
An integrated Algerian platform for resource management and sustainable production
Connecting resources, data and engineering analysis to decisions, action and monitoring through the Water–Energy–Food–Ecosystems–Health nexus.
Field data · Spatial analysis · Traceable evidence

From field systems to data, from analysis to investment. FOGGARA brings together SIREP field systems, geospatial analysis and traceable evidence to develop sustainable water, energy and agricultural projects.
Resource assessment, field monitoring and irrigation efficiency
Linking renewables with pumping and operating needs
Land parcel assessment and agricultural indicators
Preparing pilots, collaboration and investment opportunities
Initial need → project scoping → field verification → evaluation → decision
First contact is by email; some technical functions remain under development and validation.

This website describes the platform, its modules and user journeys. Operational maps, analyses, accounts and devices require the original application, connected data sources and readiness verification.

children.text: Foggara heritage inspires connected resource management
The oasis brings interconnected resources, organized distribution and sustainable production into one landscape.
FOGGARA carries these connections into a digital platform combining field data with engineering analysis, to inform decisions and track their effects on water, energy, food, ecosystems and health.

Reference slides with a short summary reflecting the updated architecture.
Organized water distribution inspires the connection between resources, information and responsibilities.
Sites and equipment connect with observation, analysis and evidence, followed by a decision reviewed by an authorized person.
Water decisions affect energy, production, ecosystems and health. These relationships are assessed together.
Spatial analysis starts with boundaries, coordinates and area measurements with known sources. Analyses then connect to that geometry.
Satellite acquisitions are periodic. Vegetation, water and moisture indicators retain their capture date and quality context.
Satellite indicators are compared with field measurements and laboratory results. Critical recommendations require specialist verification.
Information is observed, verified, computed, inferred or proposed, with its source and limits of use.
Alternatives are compared against water, energy, soil, constraints, costs and risks. The decision rationale is recorded.
The target architecture uses local models, internal knowledge, access permissions and audit under specialist oversight.
Project needs connect with partners’ expertise. Under the latest structure, the technical document workspace remains optional.
The reference slides are in French. Each summary explains the topic in the page language and reflects the current structure. These are design references, not proof of operational availability.
FOGGARA is the integrated digital layer of the SIREP system.

FOGGARA-DZ connects site, infrastructure and resource data with engineering expertise to identify needs, verify information, compare alternatives and support implementation and outcome monitoring. Its scope includes agriculture, energy, water and the economic and institutional actors connected to them.

The original field system: sensing and measurement, monitoring and control, pumping and irrigation equipment, renewable energy and local control, subject to equipment availability and verified safety conditions.
FOGGARA-DZ: mapping, digital twins, analysis, simulation, assisted intelligence and evidence, together with needs-to-capabilities matching and project support.

The name draws on the foggara and kasria water distribution heritage: connected resources, organized allocation and shared responsibilities. The platform extends that principle to information and decisions across five linked domains.
Five domains. One connected decision system.
Each domain has its own resources, indicators and constraints. The nexus engine compares cross-domain effects while making trade-offs, assumptions and data quality explicit.
Wells, storage and flows; water quality and salinity; irrigation demand and use efficiency.
Pumping, motors and variable-speed drives; solar generation, energy use and continuity of operation.
Soil, crops and growth stages; water needs, plant health and production planning.
Vegetation, land and biodiversity; resource pressure and the environmental effects of decisions.
Links between water, soil, food and human, animal and ecosystem health; specialist assessments remain with qualified professionals.

A proposed pump runtime depends on more than irrigation demand: it also depends on water availability and quality, pumping capacity, energy supply, soil and crop conditions, and environmental and operating constraints.
From site and measurement to project and decision.
Sites, parcels and infrastructure; boundary drawing and area measurement with source disclosure; wells, tanks, pumps, valves and sensors linked to resources and projects.
Water and soil analysis records, salinity and moisture, crop health, remote-sensing indicators, water requirements and agricultural calendars.
Generation, consumption, pumping and solar data; IoT and SCADA integration with SIREP; alerts and operating permissions.
Dynamic resource-and-demand matrices; hard constraints and preferences; explained alternatives for approval by an authorized person.
Reproducible scenarios with documented assumptions and versions; specialist assistants grounded in internal knowledge and available evidence.
Measurements, results and reports linked to their source, instrument and calibration status; review, approval and change history.
Project resources, needs, cost assumptions and risks; missing documentation, action plans and progress milestones.
Connecting project needs with engineering firms, suppliers, laboratories and experts using location, expertise, capabilities, qualifications and evidence.
Engineering services connected to platform workflows.
Contracted work requires a defined technical scope, service offer and deliverables, aligned with available capabilities, qualifications and project requirements.
Irrigation, pumping and renewable-energy studies; operating diagnostics, technical requirements and solution comparisons.
Field measurements, equipment inspection and laboratory-result organization. Report status is explicit; accredited calibration requires a qualified provider and verified accreditation.
Site and parcel characterization, spatial layers, vegetation and water indicators, and maps and reports with stated sources and dates.
Sensor and communication requirements, operating data and alerts, and monitoring/control integration studies for SIREP equipment.
Data organization, dashboards and reports; analysis rules, scenario comparisons and documented decision rationale.
Measurable field trials, technical files, implementation monitoring, and results and gaps documented before the next stage.
The agricultural parcel connects the information.

Parcel boundaries and the source of its measured area connect with soil, water and crop characteristics, weather, moisture and energy. Every result retains its location, period, source and calculation method.
These describe the intended functional scope. Indicators and recommendations are not presented as live when a suitable provider, measurement or model is unavailable.
Parcels, crops and irrigation needs; measurements, operations and recommendations for their holdings.
Infrastructure, resource use, equipment performance, alerts and intervention plans.
Technical files, needs, progress evidence and delegated access to relevant documents.
Studies, measurements, analyses and reports with explicit expertise and review responsibility.
Documented capabilities and responses to defined needs without public exposure of project data.
Authorized information, readiness gaps, assumptions and risks within access granted by the project owner.
Programmes, pilots and research; authorized indicators and reports within their delegated scope.
Data access is limited to authorized parties, with organizational separation, role- and project-based permissions, and a record of access, edits and approvals.
A connected chain from resource to learning.

Identify the resource and need, structure data, analyze it and apply constraints. Alternatives undergo human review; actions are monitored and outcomes compared with expectations. Evidence informs the next cycle.
Every information item has a status. Every decision has an owner.
A reading or event collected from an identified source.
Information checked within a stated scope.
A result with documented inputs and calculation method.
An explained inference with limits and confidence.
An alternative or action awaiting review and approval.
Evidence carries its source, date, spatial scope, unit and quality; instrument and calibration status where relevant; calculation method or model version; reviewer and authorized approver.

Specialist agents support evidence, engineering, calculation, GIS, risk, regulatory review, contracts, projects, investment, matching, simulation, monitoring and assurance. Tasks follow permission boundaries. Consequential decisions and equipment activation remain with authorized people and safety controls.

The target includes local hosting and processing, local models and internal knowledge retrieval, access control, audit trails and data minimization. Algerian data-protection requirements must be reviewed before operation; this description is not a compliance certificate.
Technical support and organized information for decisions.
The journey starts with project assessment and needs identification, then evidence, studies and an implementation plan. Readiness gaps are visible before commercial or financing decisions.
Site, resources, equipment, measurements, studies and constraints, with actions, responsibilities and verification milestones.
Investment needs, costs, scenarios, assumptions and risks. Each financial estimate retains its source and review date.
Traceability of specifications, measurements and technical acceptance; needs, offers, commitments and delivery. This is a verification chain, not financial backing or insurance.

Documents, sharing permissions, file versions and technical meeting records organized as needed. An investment data room is not required for core services. Registration, financing and formal approval remain with competent institutions, including AAPI where applicable.

An engineering, technical-services and digital-solutions enterprise based around the project in Laghouat, Algeria. Its vision connects field systems and digital tools for sustainable resource management and production. SIREP stands for Smart Integrated Regulation
Field-pilot sites; engineering firms, laboratories and universities; equipment and technology integration; project support and financing based on reviewable technical files.
Turn a practical need into a defined project.
Talk to SIREP about technical studies, field pilots and the development of FOGGARA-DZ.
Farms and organisations: tell us about the site, resource or equipment and the problem to assess.
Engineering firms, labs, universities and suppliers: propose a pilot site or technical contribution.
Investors and strategic partners: discuss product development or a clearly scoped field pilot.
A clear scope. Evidence you can review.
The project connects SIREP field monitoring and control with FOGGARA analysis and decision support. Discussions can cover product development, pilot equipment or service partnerships.
The problem, application site, each party’s contribution and validation plan.
Budget, product readiness, risks, rights, responsibilities and milestones.
A non-confidential introduction, an exploratory meeting, then a written scope and appropriate document exchange.
An initial discussion is not a public investment offer or a promise of returns. Funding and partnerships require review and a written agreement.
From first contact to a practical next step
Name or organisation, role, location and a short problem statement.
Identify the information needed and the technical or investment questions.
A meeting or scope proposal; timing and costs are agreed directly.
Send a short introduction and your preferred reply channel. Do not include passwords, financial data or confidential documents in your first message.
The button opens your email application. Nothing is sent until you send the message there. You can also use the address below directly.
This website presents the project and its architecture. Availability of individual functions and services is confirmed during the discussion.
Can I propose a pilot site?
Yes. Share the location, available resources and objective. Scope, data and equipment requirements will be agreed together.
How can I protect my idea?
Start with a non-confidential summary. Discuss confidentiality terms before sharing sensitive information.
Define the need. Establish the next step.
Share your role, project location, resources or equipment and the problem to address. The study or pilot scope, required data and expected deliverables can then be defined.
